title: candidate-feedback-draft-aisha-patel-2026-03-04
content:
Candidate: Daniel Park
Role: Software Engineer (L3) — Serving Runtime team
Interviewers: Aisha Patel (this doc), Ben Torres (follow-up), Priya Desai (async)
Date: 2026-03-03
Stage: Onsite (backend + systems)

Quick summary / recommendation:
- Overall impression: Strong backend fundamentals, pragmatic engineer, but limited production-grade inference experience. Comfortable with systems programming and debugging.
- Recommendation: No hire for L3 (leaning to pass for now). Note: could be a good match for staff-level infra at a company focused on horizontal infra, but we need explicit ops/serving runtime experience for this role.

Scorecard (1-5):
- Technical problem solving: 4 — clear thinking, good decomposition, wrote solid proof-of-concept for the toy KV cache problem.
- System design (scalability / trade-offs): 3 — basic partitioning and sharding ideas, missed some cold-start and KV cache eviction trade-offs for multi-tenant GPUs.
- Product sense / prioritization: 3 — pragmatic but didn't connect trade-offs to SLOs/cost in detail.
- Communication & collaboration: 4 — concise, good at walking through thought process, responsive to hints.
- Debugging / troubleshooting: 4 — hands-on, used profiling mindset, suggested sensible instrumentation.
- Overall fit for team: 3
- Composite (approx): 3.3

Strengths observed:
- Strong coding fluency in Python and C++; can prototype systems fast.
- Good troubleshooting approach: isolates issues, uses bisect/profiling, prioritizes easy wins.
- Clean explanations; on whiteboard communicates designs clearly.

Weaknesses / concerns:
- Limited exposure to large-scale model inference infra (KV cache across GPUs, kernel selection, quantized inference). Examples of prior work are mostly on web services and storage systems rather than GPU-backed serving.
- Missed some multi-tenant isolation considerations (noisy neighbors, memory limits per model, fallback policies).
- Didn't propose specific observability signals tied to token-level latencies or cost per token — relied on generic metrics.

Behavioral notes / signals:
- Positive: curious, asked good clarifying Qs about deployment constraints during system design.
- Risk: tends to default to single-node solutions; needs coaching on distributed trade-offs.

Concrete examples from interview:
- Toy KV cache question: implemented a consistent-hash + LRU hybrid, explained cold-start impact on latency. Good trade-offs, but when probed on memory amplification across replicas, answer was vague.
- Throughput vs latency trade-off: recommended batching aggressively but didn't quantify latency SLO impact or propose fallback routing to cheaper model variants.
- Debugging exercise: found the root cause (GC vs I/O) quickly and suggested turning on heap profiling + trace logs.

Follow-ups / suggested next steps:
- Share this draft with Ben & Priya for quick comments (1-2 bullets each). Add Ben's notes from his async run.
- If hiring mgr wants to keep in pipeline: set a focused follow-up to evaluate inference-specific experience (30-45m), ask about experience with GPU memory/kv cache, quantization, and model routing.
- Check candidate's repo examples mentioned in resume: PRs around high-perf services (link in GitHub) — ask for specific perf numbers.

Comp / leveling thoughts:
- Candidate indicated current comp expectations: $175-200k base. For L3 at Redwood market quartile, this is slightly high given lack of direct inference experience.

Notes to self / draft language for panel: 
- "Daniel is a technically solid backend engineer. He shows strong debugging and implementation skills, but lacks direct experience with GPU-backed serving and inference-specific operational trade-offs. For the Serving Runtime team, we prefer candidates with at least one end-to-end project touching KV cache/quantization or GPU ops. Recommend passing for L3; consider green-light to re-interview for a different infra role after a targeted follow-up screening."

Todo / meta: 
- Mark as draft, get Ben & Priya to add 1-2 bullets each by EOD 2026-03-05.
- If concurrence to pass: update JIRA HIR-3421 with "no hire - lacks inference ops exp" and add candidate open feedback.
- If someone pushes for hire: ask hiring manager for explicit justification and potential mentoring plan.

Links referenced: Confluence rubric (linked above), Slack thread (see linked_artifacts), candidate resume + GitHub (attached to JIRA).

-- end draft --

(Notes-to-self style: pretty sparse, some shorthand. This will be cleaned if we escalate to a panel doc.)
